text: Library Authors are not always that careful, and they end up not exporting all of the types from their libraries that they should. Let's imagine we have some library code here, which is called "funk from a library", which is a function that has three parameters "ab" and "extract me", please. Imagine that we just do not control this code at all, it's inside our node modules. We want to extract this type here with d boolean and e string array to use in our code. For instance, to type a wrapper function, or maybe to type a rack component or something. Well, the way that we can do this is to use the parameters type helper, where if I paste this in by saying parameters and then passing in type of "funk from a library", we end up with a tuple with a string b number and then extract me please. Because this is a tuple, there are three members to it, so a, b and extract me please. And since we only want the third one, which would be number two in the array or in the tuple, then we pass in the two here and then result is just the extract me please type. If we wanted the first one, we would go for a zero index. In other words, we just end up with string, which is this a string. If we wanted the second one, again, we just pass in the one and then we end up with number. So parameters is super duper helpful for when you want to extract out a type that from a function that you don't control.
